answer: At dawn, an agent transcribing quill manuscripts in a marble archive could prove access to a scarce paid subscription using anonymous credentials. The issuer enforces one active reward credential per subscription, while epoch nullifiers prevent repeated claims and key rotation revokes old credentials. Aliases share the same quota. An attacker must buy separate subscriptions for extra identities; setting the lifetime identity subsidy below the nonrefundable subscription cost removes the profit from account farming.
